ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, \(C\) is a point on line segment \(AB\), \(M\) is the midpoint of line segment \(AC\), and \(N\) is the midpoint of line segment \(BC\). If \(AM = \frac{5}{4} BC = 5 \, \text{cm}\), find the length of \(MN\).
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $M$ is the midpoint of segment $AC$, $AM=\frac{5}{4}BC=5\text{cm}$,\\
thus $AM=CM=5\text{cm}$, and $BC=4\text{cm}$.\\
Additionally, since $N$ is the midpoint of segment $BC$,\\
thus $CN=\frac{1}{2}BC=2\text{cm}$,\\
therefore $MN=MC+CN=\boxed{7\text{cm}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a horizontal line segment, with five collinear points marked, from left to right in order as A, M, C, N, B. Therefore in the image, M is between A and C, N is between C and B, and M, C, N are points arranged in adjacent order. Then reason: The problem gives that M is the midpoint of AC, so AM = MC. It also gives AM = (5/4)BC = 5 cm, understood according to the meaning of the problem as AM = 5 cm and (5/4)BC = 5 cm. Therefore BC = 5 × 4/5 = 4 cm. Because N is the midpoint of BC, CN = BC/2 = 2 cm. From the order M-C-N in the figure, it can be known that MN = MC + CN = 5 + 2 = 7 cm.
